text:
Alex Iafallo scored on the power play against Vancouver on Thursday, his fourth goal of the season, and the Jets have won two straight after losing nine. He's been one of Winnipeg's more productive depth players: 4 goals on 2.74 expected, a shooting rate that will cool.

The on-ice picture is better than you'd think. The Jets take 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Iafallo at five on five, eight points better than without him, and they've scored 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there. So the shooting luck has gone one way and the team luck the other.

That clashes with Evolving-Hockey's read from last season, which had his team creating fewer chances with him on (bottom 4% of forwards). One of those seasons is the outlier, and 17 games is the smaller sample. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 59% of his shots come off the rush. He's 32, undrafted out of Minnesota Duluth, with 420 games in Los Angeles before Winnipeg. We project about 15 goals. His clutch numbers (0.88 wins added from goals) rank 81st of 500, a sign his goals have come when they mattered.
headline: Iafallo's goals hide a problem
